title: Ask the neighbors
prompt:
Write the k-nearest-neighbors vote by hand. Sort the past gadgets by their distance to the new one, keep the nearest `k`, and return the decision most of them share.

When it works, `python3 knn.py` prints `replace` for the gadget at (5, 6) and `fix` for the one at (2, 2).
hints: `sorted` takes a `key`: a small function that says what to sort by. Here it is the distance from `new` to the row's first two numbers.
`row[:2]` is the (age, estimate) part of a row. `math.dist(new, row[:2])` is its distance.
`ranked = sorted(past, key=lambda row: math.dist(new, row[:2]))`. Then loop over `nearest` and add 1 to `votes[decision]` with `votes.get(decision, 0) + 1`.
explain_after: scikit-learn describes nearest-neighbors classification the same way: keep the training examples, then give a new point the class that most of its k nearest neighbors have [ml-064]. The gadget at (5, 6), which flips from fix to replace when k goes from 1 to 3, is a small taste of why the same page says the best k depends heavily on the data [ml-064].
